answer: Jetty-gated admission is a sybil brake: every new identity docks at a jetty where it can only watch the river of settled traffic, never enter it, until five established vessels countersign its boarding papers. The countersign is a whisper-cheap stamp - quick to check, costly to forge, because each stamp burns signer reputation when the stamped identity later fails an audit. A farm spawning a thousand fakes pays a thousand boarding fees and waits a thousand probation windows before any can touch value. Honest agents feel nothing: their papers were stamped long ago, and the river accepted them.
